proof.text:
We first verify the unit for the quotient identification, rather than infer it from naturality alone. Put $Z=\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and $L_q=-\otimes_Z^{\mathbf L}R_q$. For $q=m,n$, take a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to F[0]$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Locally on the site, $0\to Z\xrightarrow{q}Z\to R_q\to0$ is the usual exact integer sequence. Flatness of each $P^j$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] gives a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to P\xrightarrow{q}P\to P\otimes_ZR_q\to0$, since locally tensoring with $R_q$ is quotienting by $q$. Its triangle [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] and cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] give
$$F\xrightarrow{q}F\xrightarrow{H^0(j)}H^0(P\otimes_ZR_q)\longrightarrow H^1(P)=0.$$
The K-flat computation [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and normalized unit formula [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] identify $j:P\to P\otimes_ZR_q$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, with the unit. Therefore the cokernel identification $H^0(L_qF)=F/qF$ sends that unit to the quotient $\pi_q$. This is precisely the quotient identification used in the statement: it is the single-cohomology identification induced by this cokernel, and equality of the resulting maps $F[0]\to(F/qF)[0]$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful].

proof.text:
Write $Z=\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$, $L_q=-\otimes_Z^{\mathbf L}R_q$ and $E=-\otimes_{R_m}^{\mathbf L}R_n$. Denote their units by $\eta^q$ and $\epsilon$. For $K=F,B_0$ write $\alpha_{q,K}:L_qK\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{q,K}$ for the identifications of [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction], where $T_{q,F}=\bar F_q[0]$ and $T_{q,B_0}=H_q[1]$. To apply that lemma, use the split extension $0\to B_0\to B_0\oplus F\to F\to0$; its extra extension hypothesis is thereby satisfied. By Step 1, $(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_{q,F})\eta^q_F$ is $\pi_q:F\to F/qF$; the stated torsion normalization gives $(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_{q,B_0})\eta^q_{B_0}=\kappa_q$. Set $c_K=\alpha_{n,K}\,a_K\,E(\alpha_{m,K}^{-1}):E(T_{m,K})\to T_{n,K}$. By the composite-unit identity of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] and naturality of the units of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction],
$$(\operatorname{Res}c_K)(\operatorname{Res}\epsilon_{T_{m,K}})(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_{m,K})\eta^m_K=(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_{n,K})\eta^n_K.$$
All terms in this equality are restricted to $D(Z)$; before that restriction, $c_K$ is a morphism in $D(R_n)$ and $\epsilon$ is a morphism in $D(R_m)$.

source.place: Tags 0D6D and 07A6, applied to Z → R_m → R_n; normalized one-exponent identifications from the cited existing node. Agent notation and composite-unit calculation.

proof.text: The one-term complexes $\bar F_m[0]$ and $H_m[0]$ are bounded above with flat terms by hypothesis, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The K-flat computation of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] therefore identifies $E(\bar F_m[0])$ with $(\bar F_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n)[0]$, and $E(H_m[1])$ with $(H_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n)[1]$. The unit and transpose formulas of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] apply to these actual flat-term complexes: the unit is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and the transpose of a map $g$ is $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,g(x)$. These formulas also hold after shifting: termwise scalar extension commutes with shift, and both shifted differentials have the same minus sign.

proof.text:
Let $\rho:\bar F_m\to\bar F_n$ send $f\bmod mF$ to $f\bmod nF$. It is defined since $mF\subset nF$, and $\rho\pi_m=\pi_n$. Put $v_F=(\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}c_F)\epsilon_{\bar F_m}$ in $D(R_m)$. Step 2 says that the maps $v_F\alpha_{m,F}$ and $\rho\alpha_{m,F}$ from $L_mF$ to $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\bar F_n$ have the same adjunct $\pi_n$ in $D(Z)$. The first adjunction ($Z\to R_m$) of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] is a bijection on these Hom sets, so $v_F\alpha_{m,F}=\rho\alpha_{m,F}$, hence $v_F=\rho$ since $\alpha_{m,F}$ is invertible. The second adjunction ($R_m\to R_n$), computed as in Step 3, now gives
$$c_F(\bar f\otimes\bar b)=b f\bmod nF.$$
Thus this is the map induced by $a_F$, rather than merely an abstract isomorphism of its source and target.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; agent application of the two normalized adjunction bijections and composite-unit equality of Step 2.

proof.text:
Put $d=m/n$ and define $\beta:H_m\to H_n$ by $\beta(h)=dh$. This is well defined because $n d h=m h=0$, and is $R_m$-linear after restriction of $H_n$. Consider the two short exact sequences $S_q:0\to H_q\to B_0\xrightarrow{q}B_0\to0$. The triple $(\beta,d\operatorname{id}_{B_0},\operatorname{id}_{B_0})$ is a morphism $S_m\to S_n$: the inclusion square says $d h=\beta(h)$ and the multiplication square says $n d=m$. The naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], applied to these sequences in degree zero, gives the precise boundary equation
$$\beta[1]\,\kappa_m=\kappa_n$$
in $D(Z)$. Both boundaries are the canonical short-exact-sequence boundaries used in the normalization in the item, so the same cone convention is used on both rows.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, naturality for the displayed morphism of short exact sequences. Agent explicit comparison of the two moduli.

proof.text:
Put $v_B=(\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}c_{B_0})\epsilon_{H_m[1]}:H_m[1]\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}H_n[1]$ in $D(R_m)$. By Step 2, the adjunct of $v_B\alpha_{m,B_0}$ under $L_m\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ is $\kappa_n$. By Step 5, the adjunct of $\beta[1]\alpha_{m,B_0}$ is also $\beta[1]\kappa_m=\kappa_n$. The first adjunction bijection of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] gives $v_B\alpha_{m,B_0}=\beta[1]\alpha_{m,B_0}$, and invertibility of $\alpha_{m,B_0}$ gives $v_B=\beta[1]$. We have cancelled an isomorphism after using an adjunction bijection, not cancelled $\kappa_m$. Transposing under the second adjunction and using Step 3 shows that $c_{B_0}$ is the shift of
$$H_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n\longrightarrow H_n,\qquad h\otimes\bar b\longmapsto b d h.$$
This identifies the actual transitivity comparison and its sign. The map on $h\otimes1$ is $dh$, or $h^{m/n}$ in multiplicative notation.

proof.text: For any $R_m$-module sheaf $M$, the maps $M\otimes_{R_m}R_n\to M/nM$, $x\otimes\bar b\mapsto bx\bmod nM$, and $M/nM\to M\otimes_{R_m}R_n$, $x\bmod nM\mapsto x\otimes1$, are inverse: balancing gives $nx\otimes1=x\otimes\bar n=0$, and $(bx)\otimes1=x\otimes\bar b$. Scalars of $R_n$ lift locally to integers, so these formulas define morphisms on the presheaf tensor and descend through the sheafification of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Quotients here are sheaf cokernels, so representatives and lifts are local. With $M=F/mF$, its quotient by $nM$ is $F/nF$ because $mF\subset nF$. This proves directly that the formula in Step 4 is an isomorphism, with inverse $f\bmod nF\mapsto(f\bmod mF)\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; elementary local balanced-tensor calculation and sheafification.

proof.text: The map $\beta$ of Step 5 is locally surjective: for $t\in H_n$, surjectivity of $m:B_0\to B_0$ gives locally $z$ with $mz=t$; then $h=nz$ satisfies $dh=t$ and $mh=n t=0$. Its kernel is exactly $nH_m$: one inclusion follows from $d(ny)=my=0$ for $y\in H_m$; conversely if $h\in H_m$ and $dh=0$, surjectivity of $n$ gives locally $y$ with $ny=h$, and $my=dh=0$, so $y\in H_m$. Therefore $H_m/nH_m\xrightarrow{\beta}H_n$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. Step 7 identifies its source with $H_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n$, so this is precisely the map in Step 6. This argument uses no points of the site and no global surjectivity on sections. When $m=n$ it is the identity; when $n=1$ both quotients and both target sheaves vanish. The same formulas cover zero sheaves.

title: Modulus change of the derived quotient and torsion identifications
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a final object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $m,n\geq1$ with $n\mid m$, put $R_q=(\mathbf Z/q\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ and let $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ be the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived scalar extension with its restriction adjunction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let
$$a_K:(K\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_m)\otimes_{R_m}^{\mathbf L}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_n$$
be the canonical transitivity isomorphism of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] for the ring maps $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to R_m\to R_n$. Let $F,B_0$ be abelian sheaves such that multiplication by each of $m,n$ is injective on $F$ and surjective on $B_0$. Put $H_q=\ker(q:B_0\to B_0)$ and $\bar F_q=F/qF$. Assume that $H_m$ and $\bar F_m$ are flat $R_m$-module sheaves, meaning their tensor functors on module sheaves preserve short exact sequences [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Under the quotient and normalized torsion identifications
$$F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_q\simeq\bar F_q[0],\qquad B_0\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_q\simeq H_q[1]$$
of [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] ($q=m,n$), $a_F$ and $a_{B_0}$ induce isomorphisms
$$\bar F_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar F_n,\quad \bar f\otimes\bar b\longmapsto bf\bmod nF,$$
$$H_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n,\quad h\otimes\bar b\longmapsto b(m/n)h.$$
In multiplicative notation the second formula on $h\otimes1$ is $h\mapsto h^{m/n}$. The normalization is the one for which the scalar-extension unit on $B_0$ is the connecting morphism of $0\to H_q\to B_0\xrightarrow{q}B_0\to0$.
